book.title: Yunus Emre: A Dervish with a Good Heart (A1)

pages.title: A Great Poet
pages.content:
Yunus Emre was a great Turkish poet. He was born in Anatolia in 1240. He wrote poems in simple Turkish, and people understood them well. His poems talk about love for Allah and for Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). They teach good lessons. People read them today, too.

When Yunus was young, he went to a madrasa. A madrasa was a school. After school, he became a dervish. Dervishes lived in a dervish house with a teacher. Yunus’s teacher was Taptuk Emre. Yunus lived at the same time as Mevlana. He died in 1320.

pages.title: Open Hands
pages.content:
Dervishes looked for Allah everywhere. They looked with their eyes and with their hearts. Some dervishes had money, but they gave it to poor people. They gave their food, too. Their hands were open, and their hearts were rich.

Dervishes were kind and happy. They did not get angry quickly. They were always honest. They did not say bad things about other people. They ate a little, talked a little and slept a little. They did good work every day. This life was not easy. In one poem, Yunus said, “You cannot be a dervish.”

With a lot of money or good things.

pages.title: Straight Wood
pages.content:
Yunus went to the dervish house of Taptuk Emre. He said to his teacher, “I want to stay here and learn from you. And I want to help you.” Taptuk Emre gave Yunus a job. There was a mountain behind the dervish house. Every day, Yunus went up the mountain. He found wood there and carried it on his back. It was very hard work.

Yunus only took straight wood to the house. He never took wood that was not straight. He looked for the best wood. The wood was like his heart. Yunus worked on the wood, and he also worked on his heart. Every day, his heart was a little better.

pages.title: Forty Years on the Mountain
pages.content:
Yunus did this work for 40 years. One day, Taptuk Emre asked him, “My Yunus, why do you always take straight wood to us? Is there no other wood on the mountain?”

Yunus answered, “My teacher, this is a house of good and honest people. Wood that is not straight cannot come in here. And people who are not honest cannot come in here.”

On the mountain, Yunus was often alone. There were trees, animals and rivers. Yunus looked at nature and learned from it. He remembered Allah all the time. Everything in nature told him something about Allah.

pages.title: One Small Flower
pages.content:
One day, Taptuk Emre said to his students, “Go to the fields and get flowers for me. I will give a present for the most beautiful flowers.” The students took a lot of flowers. They ran back quickly.

Yunus came back last, in the late afternoon. He had only one daisy in his hand. Some students laughed at him. They said, “Look! He has only one small flower!”

Taptuk Emre asked, “Yunus, why did you get only one flower?”

pages.title: The Daisy Speaks
pages.content:
Yunus said, “My teacher, every flower in the fields said the name of Allah. I could not cut them. In the evening, this daisy spoke to me. It said, ‘My time is finished. Take me, dervish Yunus.’ I took only this one.”

These two stories teach us important lessons. We need to remember Allah in our hearts all the time. Every job is important. We need to do it well and in the right way. A heart with love for Allah makes our life beautiful.
